record.question: Who was the first to study vital statistics in 1661?
record.explanation: Answer B: Captain John Graunt. John Graunt’s 1662 publication on the bills of mortality is a foundational early quantitative analysis of vital statistics. The question’s “1661” likely refers to the period of his study rather than publication. Source/context note: Date phrasing is imprecise: Graunt’s famous work was published in 1662, although some sources date his study to 1661. Reference: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/series/sr_04/sr04_029.pdf; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10919065/. Verified worked solution, unofficial. Original printed wording and option order reviewed; no matching examiner key is asserted.
